content: 1. The point estimates demonstrate significant variability in both the direction and magnitude of the effect, with some confidence intervals (CIs) not overlapping. This indicates high statistical heterogeneity, as reflected by an I-squared value of 94%. 2. Cardiovascular mortality, cognitive impairment/dementia, end-stage kidney disease, adverse events, and blood pressure reduction were not reported in the studies. 3. Confidence intervals crossed the threshold of 10 per 1000 patients, suggesting the possibility of both important benefits and harms. This indicates very low certainty in the evidence. 4. One of the three included studies was observational (Bangalore), while the others were randomized controlled trials (RCTs). 5. The review reports that all included studies were at low risk of bias, but it does not provide detailed information about the risk of bias (RoB) across different domains. The ALLHAT 2005 study, which contributed over 50% of the pooled estimate weight, was judged to have an unclear risk of bias in the domain of blinding of outcome assessment in another review. 6. The trials were judged to have a high risk of bias in the domains of randomization and blinding. However, the authors did not provide detailed risk of bias assessments for each included trial. 7. Not all included studies directly compared antihypertensive monotherapy head-to-head. 8. The confidence interval crosses the line of no effect, suggesting that the difference could be significantly less or more. The extremes of the confidence interval could lead to different clinical decisions. 9. There is a very low event rate, which limits the reliability of the findings. 10. Evidence of publication bias was identified using Egger’s analysis. 11. The T-VENTURE 2009 trial was judged to have a high risk of bias in allocation concealment and blinding. However, this trial contributed less than 4% of the pooled effect estimate weight, so the risk of bias was not downgraded. 12. The funnel plot suggests the possibility of publication bias. 13. The review states that ACE inhibitors (ACEis) caused adverse events such as cough, taste disturbance, rash, and angioedema, while angiotensin receptor blockers (ARBs) frequently caused hypotension and renal dysfunction. 14. The confidence interval crosses the line of no effect, suggesting that the difference could be significantly less or more. This reflects high statistical heterogeneity, as indicated by an I-squared value of 96%. 15. The outcome is informed by indirect comparisons within a network meta-analysis. 16. The included study was judged by another review (Lin, 2017) to have a high risk of bias in the domain of selective reporting. 17. The review does not provide I-squared values or confidence intervals for individual studies to assess heterogeneity. It states that a loop-specific inconsistency approach was used to assess disagreement between direct and indirect evidence, and consistency results were considered non-significant when 95% CIs of inconsistency factors included zero or when the ratio of odds ratios (RoR) included one. 18. A 50% drop in eGFR and doubling of serum creatinine are validated surrogate markers for end-stage kidney disease (ESKD), so indirectness was not downgraded. 19. The baseline risk was not reported in the network meta-analysis. Values were abstracted directly from the included studies. 20. The confidence interval crosses the threshold of 10 per 1000 patients, suggesting the possibility of both important benefits and harms. 21. The upper value of the confidence interval is very close to the line of no effect, suggesting almost no effect or an important benefit. 22. There is a low number of events, which limits the reliability of the findings. 23. The total number of trials informing direct comparisons is three. 24. The weight of each included study was not provided. However, all included studies were judged to have a high risk of bias in the domains of blinding of participants, personnel, and outcome assessors. 25. The review does not provide I-squared values or confidence intervals for individual studies to assess heterogeneity. It states that a loop-specific inconsistency approach was used to assess disagreement between direct and indirect evidence, and consistency results were considered non-significant when 95% CIs of inconsistency factors included zero or when the RoR included one. 26. The confidence interval crosses the line of no effect, suggesting that the difference could be significantly less or more. 27. No direct comparison data is available for this outcome. 28. The event rate was extracted from the ALLHAT 2006 trial, but this includes events from all arms (thiazide, CCB, and ACEi). The event rate for the thiazide arm was not provided. 29. There is no direct comparison between ACE inhibitors and diuretics for the outcome of mortality. The event rate from the diuretics arm was used from the COPE 2013 trial, which included three arms: ARB, beta-blocker, and thiazide. 30. The result of this outcome is informed by the direct comparison of ACE inhibitors versus diuretics in the post hoc subgroup analysis of the ALLHAT 2006 trial. 31.
